project_type: Python 3.13 microservices with Apache Kafka event streaming, FastAPI backend, Docker Compose orchestration
build_system: pip with requirements.txt per service (no build step — interpreted Python)
test_framework: pytest 7.4+ with pytest-asyncio for async tests
build_command: N/A (interpreted Python — services run directly with python -m <service>)
verification_instructions: Run pytest for each changed module. For kafka_utils changes: pytest kafka_utils/test_kafka.py -v. For service changes: pytest tests/test_<service>.py -v. For integration: docker compose up --build -d && docker compose ps to verify all containers healthy.
environment_constraints: Never restart kafka/zookeeper manually — docker compose manages lifecycle. Services consume env vars from docker-compose.yml environment blocks. Local dev uses localhost:9093 for Kafka, docker services use kafka:9092.
contribution_requirements: Tests must pass (pytest tests/ -v). Services must be stateless and idempotent. All Kafka topics must follow naming: <service>.<entity> (e.g., telemetry.raw, mpc.decisions). Log at INFO level for operational events, DEBUG for verbose details, ERROR for failures.
key_patterns: MessageProcessor base class in kafka_utils/utils.py for all consumer services. Services inherit from MessageProcessor, override process_message(), and call run() in main(). Services use signal handlers for graceful shutdown. All services log with Python logging module and standard format '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'. Tests use pytest fixtures and follow pattern: load data, instantiate class, assert expectations.
directory_structure: kafka_utils/ = shared Kafka client utilities. services/<name>/ = microservice entrypoints with main.py and Dockerfile. src/ = core business logic modules (forecasting, mpc, derms, compliance). tests/ = pytest test suite. data/ = dataset.csv for training. docker/ = docker config files. .agents/ = workflow artifacts.
